# External datasets

## Current experimental scope

The current human-data experiment uses Fluent Speech Commands (FSC) in
English. The project does not treat FSC as an Android corpus. The derived command-routing benchmark uses only four conservative mappings and labels all
other FSC intents as policy abstention. See
docs/ultrasmall_benchmark.md and data/external/fsc_command_benchmark_manifest.json for the current audit trail.

## LaPSMail (human PT-BR speech)

- Local archive: /home/daniel/datasets/lapsmail/MailDatabase1.0.zip
- Extracted command audio: /home/daniel/datasets/lapsmail/commands_16k/
- Derived index: [lapsmail_commands.jsonl](lapsmail_commands.jsonl)
- Provenance and checksums: [lapsmail_commands_manifest.json](lapsmail_commands_manifest.json)
- Scope: 1,100 human-recorded WAV files (44 canonical email commands x 25 speakers), 16 kHz mono.
- Split: speaker-disjoint 15/5/5.

This remains a documented auxiliary resource. It is Brazilian Portuguese and
contains real volunteer recordings, but its semantic domain is email rather
than Android. Use it for ASR/acoustic robustness and command-like speech; do
not use it as direct gold labels for the Android tool contract.

Source references: [LaPSMail dissertation](https://ppgcc.propesp.ufpa.br/Disserta%C3%A7%C3%B5es_2012/Rafael%20Santana%20Oliveira_Disserta%C3%A7%C3%A3o.pdf) and [open speech-corpora catalog entry](https://github.com/coqui-ai/open-speech-corpora).

## OpenVoiceOS intent benchmark (PT-BR text)

The directory [openvoiceos/](openvoiceos/) contains the pt-BR files from [OpenVoiceOS/intents-for-eval](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenVoiceOS/intents-for-eval): 1,000 templates, 50 keyword rules and 1,750 test utterances. It is Apache-2.0 and task-aligned with voice-assistant intent/slot evaluation. Its own documentation states that v0.2 was generated by Claude Opus under human guidance, so it is not human-participant gold data.
## Fluent Speech Commands (human English speech)

- Archive: /home/daniel/datasets/fluent_speech_commands/fluent.tar.gz
- Extracted data: /home/daniel/datasets/fluent_speech_commands/raw/fluent_speech_commands_dataset/
- Manifest: [fluent_speech_commands_manifest.json](fluent_speech_commands_manifest.json)
- Scope: 30,043 human recordings, 97 speakers, 31 intents, 16 kHz mono WAV, speaker-disjoint train/valid/test.
- License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, academic research only.

This is the best immediate English audio benchmark for command-like speech in the current transcript-routing study. Its semantics are smart-home/assistant commands, so it is suitable for the generic benchmark and future audio/ASR work—not direct gold labels for an Android contract.

Official provenance: [Fluent.ai dataset page](https://fluent.ai/fluent-speech-commands-a-dataset-for-spoken-language-understanding-research/). The local archive was obtained from a public [Hugging Face mirror](https://huggingface.co/datasets/leo19941227/fluent_speech_commands) and checked by SHA-256.

### Derived generic command-routing benchmark

- Contract: data/tools/fsc_command_benchmark.json
- Official speaker-disjoint data:
  fluent_speech_commands_command_benchmark.jsonl
- Phrase-disjoint data:
  fluent_speech_commands_command_benchmark_phrase_disjoint.jsonl
- Derivation: ../scripts/prepare_fsc_android_fc.py
- Size of each balanced derivation: 14,956 rows, 7,478 calls and 7,478
  policy abstentions.

Only activate/deactivate music and increase/decrease volume are mapped to
generic tools. The mapping is a manually specified semantic bridge,
not a source annotation. The benchmark consumes FSC transcriptions; it does
not evaluate an end-to-end ASR model.

## SLURP (human English SLU annotations)

- Checkout: /home/daniel/datasets/slurp/
- Manifest: [slurp_manifest.json](slurp_manifest.json)
- Human-origin text: 11,514 train, 2,033 devel and 2,974 test examples, with intents/entities and linked audio identifiers.
- Relevant scenarios include alarm, audio, music, calendar, email and IoT.
- Keep 	rain_synthetic.jsonl separate; it is explicitly synthetic.

Source: [SLURP repository](https://github.com/pswietojanski/slurp).
